summary.text: Luz Maria Rivas is the Democratic incumbent for California's 29th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. An electrical engineer by training, she founded the nonprofit DIY Girls, served on the Los Angeles Board of Public Works, and represented the San Fernando Valley in the California State Assembly from 2018 to 2024. In the House she serves on the Natural Resources and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Los Angeles, California, in 1974; according to her official House biography she grew up in Pacoima, raised by a single mother, and attended San Fernando High School (class of 1991).
Earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from MIT in 1995 and a master's degree in technology in education from Harvard University in 2003.
Worked as an electrical design engineer at Motorola after college.

Founded and served as executive director of DIY Girls, a nonprofit that introduces girls to technology and engineering; also co-founded KitHub and was director of research and corporate partnerships at Iridescent.
Served as a commissioner on the Los Angeles Board of Public Works.

Served in the California State Assembly from 2018 to 2024; her House biography says she secured over $70 million in state funding for projects in the San Fernando Valley and worked to expand computer science and climate change education.
Was elected to the U.S. House in 2024 and took office on January 3, 2025, succeeding Tony Cárdenas; her House office says she is the first Latina to represent the district.

Serves on the House Natural Resources Committee (Energy and Minerals; Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries subcommittees) and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Research and Technology; Investigations and Oversight subcommittees).
Was elected by her peers as the Freshman Leadership Representative in House Democratic Leadership for the 119th Congress, and co-chairs the Congressional STEM Education Caucus.
